newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end thin bourse trade lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares end thin bourse trade lower.

text.p: German shares ended a listless bourse trading day lower on Thursday, with dealers saying many players had closed their books for the year and the market was drifting in a range.
Even news that the Bundesbank had left interest rates unchanged, as expected by most analysts, failed to moved the share market.
The DAX index of 30 top German shares ended down 13 points, or 0.46 percent, at 2,807.75 points.
Thursday is the last trading day for the December DAX futures contract and dealers said that had led to some volatility in the day's dealings as players moved to cover their futures positions.
They said the expiry of futures contracts on individual shares had also led to volatility in stocks such as industrial group Daimler, electronics group Siemens and insurer Allianz.
Dealers said the market had been supported by strength on Wall Street and a firm dollar.

One of the day's most heavily traded stock was Commerzbank, Germany's third largest bank, which dropped 67 pfennigs to trade at 38.75 marks, erasing most of the gains it made in recent days on unconfirmed merger speculation.
